frontMatter.welcome:
Welcome to PennEngineering & Manufacturing Corp. ("PennEngineering") (Group). We are delighted to welcome you to our global organization and are pleased that you have chosen to build your career with us.
At PennEngineering (Group), we recognize that our employees are the foundation of our success. Through innovation, collaboration, integrity, and a shared commitment to excellence, our people help deliver the high-quality engineered fastening solutions and technologies that customers around the world rely upon every day.
Whether you contribute through manufacturing, engineering, operations, customer service, administration, supply chain, sales, or support functions, your efforts play an important role in maintaining our reputation for quality, reliability, and customer satisfaction. Every employee contributes to advancing our mission and supporting the long-term success of the Company.
This handbook has been developed to help you understand our workplace culture, values, employment practices, and the resources available to support your professional journey. We are excited to have you as part of the PennEngineering team and look forward to achieving continued success together.
PennEngineering's mission is to provide innovative, reliable, and precision-engineered fastening solutions that enable customers to improve manufacturing efficiency, product performance, and assembly effectiveness across a wide range of industries.
We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of quality, safety, ethical business conduct, and operational excellence. Through continuous improvement, technological innovation, and responsible business practices, we strive to create long-term value for our customers, employees, suppliers, communities, and other stakeholders.

- Review the Contents Thoroughly: Take the time to read and understand the information contained in this handbook to become familiar with your rights, responsibilities, and workplace expectations.
- Use It as a Reference Guide: Refer to this handbook whenever you need clarification regarding Company policies, employment practices, or workplace procedures.
- Stay Informed of Updates: PennEngineering may revise this handbook periodically to reflect changes in business practices, legal requirements, or organizational needs. Employees are encouraged to remain informed regarding any updates communicated by the Company.
If you have any questions regarding the information contained in this handbook or require additional clarification, please contact your supervisor, manager, or a member of the Human Resources team. This handbook is intended to support a positive, rewarding, and successful employment experience at PennEngineering.
At PennEngineering, we are committed to maintaining a workplace that promotes accountability, fairness, inclusion, employee wellbeing, and operational excellence. This section outlines the Company's global expectations regarding working practices, compensation, employee benefits, wellbeing, and leave entitlements.
As a global organization, PennEngineering operates across multiple jurisdictions. Accordingly, employees and managers are required to comply with applicable local laws, regulations, collective bargaining agreements, employment contracts, and country-specific policies. Where local requirements provide greater employee protections or benefits than those described in this Handbook, the local requirements shall prevail.

chapters.title: Confidentiality
chapters.text:
- Reports are handled with discretion and shared only with individuals who have a legitimate business need to know.
- If requested, reports will be treated confidentially to the extent possible and in accordance with applicable laws.
- Anonymous reporting may be made through appropriate reporting channels where permitted.
## Reporting Channels
Employees and stakeholders are encouraged to first discuss concerns with their immediate supervisor or manager whenever appropriate.
Concerns may also be reported through the following channels:
## Line Manager or Supervisor
## Human Resources Representative
## PennEngineering Speak Up Hotline
- Phone: 215-766-1000
- Email: speakup@pemnet.com
Reports may be submitted confidentially and, where appropriate, anonymously. The Speak Up contact information is displayed through Company Speak Up posters and other internal communication channels.
## Review and Investigation Process
- Receipt of Concern: Concerns submitted through the available reporting channels are documented and acknowledged, where possible.
- Initial Assessment: The appropriate Company representatives review the concern to determine the nature, urgency, and required course of action.
- Investigation: Matters requiring further review are investigated by designated personnel while maintaining fairness, objectivity, and confidentiality.
- Corrective Action: Where concerns are substantiated, appropriate corrective and preventive measures are implemented.
- Closure: To the extent appropriate and permissible, the reporting individual may be informed that the matter has been reviewed and addressed.
## Continuous Improvement
- PennEngineering periodically reviews the effectiveness of the Speak Up process and reporting mechanisms.
- Trends and lessons learned from reported concerns may be used to strengthen internal controls, workplace practices, and employee awareness initiatives.
- Employees and managers receive periodic communication and training regarding their responsibilities under the PennEngineering Code of Conduct and the importance of raising concerns in good faith.
## nvestigation, Remediation & Corrective Action Process
PennEngineering is committed to addressing concerns promptly, fairly, and consistently. The Company strives to provide a safe, inclusive, ethical, and respectful workplace and takes all reports of misconduct seriously. This process outlines how concerns are reviewed, investigated, and resolved following a report made through established reporting channels.
As a global organization, PennEngineering conducts investigations and remediation activities in accordance with applicable local laws, regulations, collective agreements, and Company policies. Where local legal requirements provide greater protections or impose additional obligations, the local requirements shall prevail.
## Scope
This process applies to employees, contractors, temporary workers, agency personnel, suppliers, and other stakeholders interacting with PennEngineering.
Concerns covered under this process may include, but are not limited to:
- Workplace harassment, bullying, discrimination, and retaliation;
- Health and safety concerns or unsafe working conditions;
- Labour and human rights violations, including concerns relating to forced labour, child labour, working conditions, or unfair treatment;
- Ethics and compliance concerns, including fraud, bribery, corruption, theft, conflicts of interest, or misuse of Company assets;
- Violations of the Code of Conduct or Company policies; and
- Any other concern reported through PennEngineering's Speak Up and Reporting Concerns process
## nvestigation and Remediation Process
## ntake and Initial Assessment
Concerns raised through PennEngineering's Speak Up channels, Human Resources, management, or other approved reporting mechanisms are reviewed promptly upon receipt.
- Where appropriate and feasible, acknowledgment of receipt may be provided to the reporting individual.
- Initial assessments are conducted to understand the nature of the concern, determine potential risks, and identify the appropriate individuals responsible for the review.
- All concerns are handled as confidentially as possible and in accordance with applicable legal requirements.
- PennEngineering strictly prohibits retaliation against individuals who raise concerns, participate in investigations, or support the review process in good faith.
## nvestigation and Fact-Finding
- Investigations are conducted by appropriately designated personnel, which may include Human Resources, Legal, Compliance, Internal Audit, Environmental Health and Safety (EHS), or other qualified individuals depending on the nature of the concern.
- External investigators or specialists may be engaged where necessary to ensure independence, expertise, or legal compliance.
- Relevant information may be collected and reviewed, including:
- Witness statements;
- Documents and records;
- System data and communications;
